newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KAL delays second Amsterdam freighter.
newsitem.headline: KAL delays second Amsterdam freighter.

text.p: Korean Air is delaying the introduction of a second freighter into Schiphol Amsterdam airport, Korean Air's Amsterdam cargo manager, Mike Zimmerman said.

Initially, the second freighter was set to enter the Amsterdam market in July for the summer season and then this introduction was abandoned in favour of October for the beginning of the winter schedule, he told Reuters.
He said that a winter schedule introduction is also unlikely, and he does not expect to see the launch of the additional freighter operation until spring 1997.

Zimmerman added that the main reason the second freighter has been postponed is because volume levels from Korea to Amsterdam are weak. The second freighter was likely to route via the Middle East or Moscow and he was hoping for a Saturday night departure, he said.
Current capacity levels are adequate with the recent introduction of a new Boeing 747-200 freighter giving the carrier an extra 15 to 20 tonnes over the previous 747-200F, he said.
The introduction of a further freighter in the winter season could lead to too much capacity ex-Amsterdam and a breakdown of the rates levels, he said.
Rates ex-Amsterdam are currently stable and relatively healthy, he added. Korean Air will not be implementing any increases ex-Amsterdam, he said.

The second freighter's arrival had been negotiated since the Dutch-Korean bilateral talks which took place in February this year. There was some debate as to whether Korean Air or Asiana, also a Korean carrier, would get the second freighter rights but Korean Air gained the rights.
